message.content: The most commonly cited “dominant” genetic trait in lions is the presence of a mane in adult males. While the mane itself is largely driven by testosterone levels, the underlying genetic predisposition for a mane is inherited in a dominant fashion—males that inherit the allele for a mane will develop one, whereas females do not typically develop a mane.
